title: Full subject identifiers, a health indicator and test support
body:
A round of changes after a review of the API, before the first release.

  • Subjects as RFC 9493 defines them. SsfSubjectIdentifier represents every format, and SsfSubject exposes all members of a complex subject. The shortcuts for user, session and email are unchanged. Matching an iss_sub identifier now requires the issuer as well as the subject, and token revocations are scoped to the issuer of the token.
  • HTTPS for the transmitter. The issuer and every endpoint in its metadata must use HTTPS; loopback addresses may use HTTP for local development, and easyssf.receiver.allow-insecure-http lifts the rule for test setups, with a warning at startup.
  • Your own event type aliases, registered in configuration or with SsfEventTypes.registerAlias, without redefining the built-in ones.
  • Typed transmitter metadata: specVersion(), deliveryMethodsSupported(), criticalSubjectMembers(), authorizationSchemes() and defaultSubjects().
  • Immutable value objects. Tokens, subjects, stream configurations and metadata copy what they are given and cannot be changed afterwards.
  • Health indicator easyssf for Spring Boot Actuator: whether the transmitter was reached, the stream is registered and the last poll succeeded, without calling the transmitter.
  • easyssf-test: the transmitter the easyssf tests use, as a module for the tests of your own receiver.
  • Every artifact ships with a CycloneDX SBOM, a self-contained POM and an automatic module name.

The schema of the EASYSSF_REVOCATION table gained an ISSUER column; nothing was released yet, so there is no migration.

title: Welcome to easyssf.org
body:
easyssf has a home. The project is a Java library and a Spring Boot 4.1 starter that turn an application into a receiver for the OpenID Shared Signals Framework: it verifies Security Event Tokens, rejects the access tokens and ends the sessions a CAEP event revokes, and hands every event to your own handlers.

Where things stand:

  • The receiver library has no framework dependencies; the Spring Boot starter covers the servlet stack, resource servers and OIDC clients.
  • Tested against the SSF transmitter of Keycloak 26.8 and the receiver test plans of the OpenID conformance suite.
  • The code is experimental and not yet published to Maven Central. Build it from source with ./mvnw install.

The source is on GitHub.
